item.title: Plato 0.4.3
item.description:
Plato 0.4.3

A reliability release: fixes for push-to-talk and voice edge cases, a tidier panel, and a large internal cleanup.

Fixed

  • A quick tap can't leave the mic open. A very short push-to-talk press now always closes the mic, and voice Captions stay in the order they were spoken.
  • Escape and re-press at the turn boundary. Pressing Escape or push-to-talk at the moment a turn ends no longer brings back the cancelled turn or its Draft.
  • No stuck "writing…". Interrupting Plato while it writes to the Pad by voice no longer leaves the status showing "writing…" forever.
  • Long conversations keep rolling. Releasing push-to-talk while Plato is still connecting no longer stops the Conversation from rolling over to a fresh session later.
  • API-key settings stay separate. On the API-Key Path, Plato no longer sends ChatGPT-only Fast Mode and Reasoning settings, and it forgets the previous account's model list when you change credentials.

Polish

  • The panel uses one consistent spacing rhythm, panel-sized Geist buttons that look clearly disabled when unavailable, and less filler text.
  • Big internal cleanup and new tests around the conversation engine, which makes future fixes safer.

Permissions, stored keys, and your sign-in all carry over. You don't need to grant or enter anything again.

item.title: Plato 0.4.2
item.description:
Plato 0.4.2

A hardening release: a sweep of small fixes to the voice conversation and the overlay, and a tighter app under the hood.

Fixed

  • Voice replies always play in order. The audio of a spoken reply is now forwarded strictly in sequence, so a busy moment can no longer garble the start of a sentence.
  • No stray words from a finished turn. Caption text arriving late from a previous reply is now dropped instead of slipping into the current one.
  • Push-to-talk at turn boundaries. A press landing at exactly the wrong instant around the start or end of a turn could leave the mic state confused; those windows are now guarded.
  • Crisper overlay after display changes. The Trailing Cursor and its listening ring redraw correctly after the screen setup changes — a display plugged in or removed, or a resolution switch.

Hardening

  • Updates got stricter: an update feed that fails signature validation is rejected immediately, with no grace period.
  • Test-only plumbing is now compiled out of shipped builds entirely.
  • The locally downloaded speech-recognition model is verified against pinned checksums before it is ever loaded.
  • Plato's own telemetry file is readable only by your user account, and shipped builds record reply lengths, never words.

Permissions, stored keys, and your sign-in all carry over — nothing to re-grant or re-enter.
